claims.text: The funding is for conference support.
There are three streams of conference support.
Stream A offers up to £200 for travel and accommodation for Genetics Society or Special Interest Group meetings.
Stream B offers up to £500 for non-Society genetics conferences.
Stream B offers up to £750 for two Adelphi Genetics Forum co-sponsored awards a year for PhD students only.
Stream C offers up to £300 for registration for virtual conferences.
The grants support attendance at conferences on research in Genetics.
The grants are for Genetics Society junior scientist members.

claims.text: Scheme (A) is open to undergraduate, Master’s and PhD student members of The Society.
Scheme (A) is open to postdoctoral scientist members of The Society within six years of their PhD viva.
Scientists who obtained their PhD more than six years ago are not eligible for Scheme (A).
Schemes (B) & (C) are open to PhD student members within six years of their PhD viva.
Schemes (B) & (C) are open to postdoctoral scientist members within six years of their PhD viva.
Undergraduate or Master’s students are not eligible for Schemes (B) & (C).
Scientists who obtained their PhD more than six years ago are not eligible for Schemes (B) & (C).
Schemes (B) & (C) are open to members with a UK base wishing to attend conferences outside of the UK.
Schemes (B) & (C) are open to non-UK-based members wishing to attend a conference in the UK.
Applications from bases outside the UK for conference attendance outside the UK cannot be considered for Schemes (B) & (C).
A maximum of one grant per two years will be awarded for applications to Scheme (B) or (C).
Applicants must present a poster or give a talk at the conference they wish to attend.
Supervisors providing support letters must be current members of the Genetics Society.
Supervisors should include their membership number in the supporting letter.
The supervisor’s supporting statement must be uploaded along with the online application before the deadline.
Grant recipients will be asked to write a short report that may be published in the Genetics Society Newsletter.
Grants up to £200 are available for travel and essential overnight accommodation for Scheme (A).
There is no limit to the frequency that Scheme (A) grants can be applied for.
Grants of up to £500 are available to attend conferences in the area of Genetics, which are not run by the Genetics Society or one of their SIGs (Scheme B).
Up to two (Scheme B) Conference grants per year will be co-sponsored by the Adelphi Genetics Forum.
Adelphi Genetics Forum co-sponsored awards can provide up to £750.
Applicants for an Adelphi Genetics Forum co-sponsored award should request between £500 and £750.
The Adelphi Genetics Forum co-sponsored award is only open to registered PhD student members who will take up the award before their PhD graduation date.
If unsuccessful for the Adelphi Genetics Forum co-sponsored award, applications will be automatically considered for a standard stream B grant for which a maximum of £500 can be awarded.
Grants of up to £300 are available to cover registration costs for virtual conferences (Scheme C).
The virtual conference grant is available to UK-based members to enable attendance at a genetics-related virtual conference based either in the UK or elsewhere.
The virtual conference grant is available to non-UK-based members to attend a UK-based Genetics related virtual conference.
Applications should be submitted in time for one of the bi-monthly deadlines: 1st day of February, April, June, August, October and December.
Applications should be made by logging into the mySociety membership portal.
Once logged in, select “Me and the GS” followed by “Grants” and then choose the Junior Scientist Conference Grant.
The conference must take place AFTER the application deadline.
For Genetics Society and Special Interest Group (SIG) meetings, applications should be submitted online before the registration deadline of the meeting.
Queries regarding the application process or submission difficulties can be directed to theteam@genetics.org.uk.
